## Plan document present and linked

Pass. The required plan exists at [dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:1) and is linked as the planning issue’s `design` document. The linked investigation and research documents are also present and substantive.

## Completeness against the criteria

Blocking failure. REQ-01 through REQ-08 and REQ-10 through REQ-11 are addressed with concrete acceptance criteria. However, the plan does not implement the pre-tag timing required by `[hard]` REQ-09.

The scope requires the stable-recency comparison “immediately before the v1.0 tag” ([scope brief, line 23](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/v1-production-readiness-scope-brief.md:23)). The plan instead describes a “tag-time” or “release” check ([plan, lines 110–116](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:110)) and permits candidate assembly only after the exact `v1.0.0` tag already exists ([plan, lines 147–153](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:147)). No pre-tag command, protected tag-creation procedure, or evidence handoff is defined. A failure at that point would require changing the commit and replacing the release tag.

## Technical soundness and architectural fit

Blocking failure in the OCI release design.

The server and Docker application architecture is otherwise accurately grounded: `jit-server` validates the existing `.jit` directory, nests routes under `/api`, and uses embedded web assets ([main.rs, lines 61–129](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/crates/server/src/main.rs:61)); `/api/health` is correct ([routes.rs, lines 33–73](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/crates/server/src/routes.rs:33)); and the empty-asset build hazard is real ([build.rs, lines 4–18](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/crates/server/build.rs:4)).

The OCI contract, however, combines requirements without specifying a supported round trip. It requires one archive carrying max provenance and an SBOM, loading and smoking that exact archive, and later copying it to GHCR without changing its authoritative digest ([plan, lines 186–193](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:186), [lines 223–235](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/.agents/worktrees/agent-8b05a612/dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md:223)). Docker’s documented local image store does not support loaded attestations; `load: true` omits them, while attached attestations normally require registry-compatible image/index handling ([Docker attestation documentation](https://docs.docker.com/build/ci/github-actions/attestations/)). The plan does not select an OCI-capable runtime/copy tool, distinguish the runnable manifest digest from the attested index digest, or define how digest preservation is verified. An engineer must re-derive this load-bearing release architecture.

## Decomposition and dependencies

The issue-task DAG is otherwise coherent: remediation precedes audit enforcement; version alignment serializes manifest changes; the replacement Docker image precedes topology removal; candidate assembly precedes npm staging; and rehearsal precedes public publication.

The pre-tag gate omission is nevertheless an ordering gap: there is no leaf responsible for validating MSRV recency and authorizing creation of the immutable `v1.0.0` tag before tag-triggered candidate work begins.

## Risks and actionability

Blocking failure. The risk table covers dependency remediation, npm ownership, workflow failure propagation, Docker runtime behavior, external epics, and partial publication. It does not mitigate:

- Failure of the stable-recency check after the release tag has already been created.
- Loss or mutation of OCI attestations/digests across archive export, runtime smoke, and registry publication.

Both are load-bearing release-identity questions and need explicit decisions and executable mechanisms.

## Prior review feedback

All three prior blockers were substantively addressed:

- The clean-room rehearsal now precedes every public v1 channel mutation.
- OIDC is proved with supported `npm stage publish`, followed by staged-package inspection and 2FA approval.
- A shared static-and-dynamic workflow verification harness is now defined with controlled failure injection and disposable fixtures.

The present failures are separate from those prior findings.

## Findings

1. **F1 — High, blocking:** `[hard]` REQ-09 requires the stable-recency comparison immediately before creating `v1.0.0`, but the plan only defines tag-time/release checks after the exact tag has entered candidate assembly. Add an explicit pre-tag gate and immutable SHA/evidence handoff so a failed recency check never requires moving a release tag. File: `dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md`, line 147. Reference: `@/issue/8b05a612/requirement/REQ-09`.
2. **F2 — High, blocking:** The exact OCI candidate contract is under-specified and is incompatible with the ordinary Docker local-load path: the plan requires attached max-provenance/SBOM attestations, exact-archive runtime loading, and digest-preserving later publication without naming an OCI-capable load/copy mechanism or defining subject versus index digests. Select and test the registry/archive transport and digest model explicitly. File: `dev/active/8b05a612-plan.md`, line 186. References: `@/issue/8b05a612/requirement/REQ-05`, `@/issue/8b05a612/requirement/REQ-07`.
